activities.anchor: The intensity scale is the first numerical habit to build
activities.caption: call the magnitude — whisper to jet
activities.name: hsDbEstimate

config.prompt: A whisper sits at about 30 dB SPL; a jet engine at close range about 140 dB SPL. Roughly how many times greater is the jet's sound pressure?
config.why: Ten million — the million-fold range between hearing threshold and pain compressed into ~110 decibels by 20·log₁₀(p / 20 µPa). +20 dB is a tenfold pressure increase; +10 dB is roughly a perceived doubling of loudness.
config.context: 20 micropascals — roughly the pressure of a mosquito at three metres — defines 0 dB SPL: a reference level, not silence.

activities.anchor: The ear is conventionally taught in three parts
activities.caption: rebuild the chain, in the order sound experiences it
activities.name: hsChainOrder

config.prompt: Each part solves a specific problem — order the links:
items: outer ear — the pinna funnels and filters; the canal resonates near 2.7 kHz
middle ear — three bones match air to fluid with about 22 dB of gain
cochlea — the basilar membrane's tonotopic map; hair cells transduce
auditory nerve and brainstem — frequency and timing maps preserved
cortex — perception: loudness, pitch, picking a voice from a party
config.why: A physics problem, a mechanical problem, and an electrochemical problem in sequence — each stage specialised, each a place the system can break.

activities.caption: pair each ear part with the problem it solves
activities.name: hsEarMatch

config.prompt: Three parts, three engineering fixes — pair them:

pairs.right: funnels sound and filters by elevation and direction — cues for 3-D localisation
resonates near 2.7 kHz, boosting exactly the consonant band
a lever system bridging the air-to-fluid mismatch with ~22 dB of gain
stiffen the chain reflexively at loud sounds — too slow against impulsive noise

config.why: Without the middle ear, over 99 per cent of the energy would reflect away at the air–fluid boundary — the same physics that makes a shout barely ripple a swimming pool.

activities.caption: pin the peak on the tonotopic map
activities.name: hsTonotopicPlace

config.prompt: An 8 kHz tone's travelling wave peaks where along the basilar membrane?
config.why: At the base: stiff and narrow there resonates high frequencies; wide and floppy at the apex for low. This tonotopic map is the single most important fact in the chapter — the audiogram's frequency axis is the cochlea's geography.
config.context: High-frequency losses cost consonant clarity first — noise damage writes its 4 kHz notch in the basal region.

activities.anchor: Resting on the membrane sits the organ of Corti
activities.caption: file the facts — inner or outer hair cells?
activities.name: hsHairBuckets

config.prompt: One row transduces; three rows amplify. File each fact:

items.label: one row — transduce motion into nerve spikes
three rows — actively amplify and sharpen the travelling wave
make the cochlea a powered, not passive, microphone
their faint emissions (OAEs) screen newborn hearing

config.why: Damage to the active amplifier distorts, compresses and smears — which is why sensorineural loss is not just 'quieter' and no simple amplification fully restores it.

activities.anchor: the ear "hears" the way a microphone records
activities.caption: true or false — the active cochlea
activities.name: hsActiveJudge

statements.s: The cochlea actively edits: outer hair cells boost weak signals and compression handles an enormous dynamic range.
statements.why: Frequency-sharp, level-dependent amplification produces ~120 dB of dynamic range despite individually limited hair cells.

statements.s: The ear hears the way a microphone records.
statements.why: It is a powered analyser, not a passive one — the brain performs pattern analysis on an already-edited signal.

statements.s: Sensorineural loss is not just 'quieter' — it distorts, compresses and smears.
statements.why: Damage to the active amplifier destroys the graceful compression, producing recruitment: loudness growing abnormally fast.

statements.s: Simple amplification fully restores what a damaged cochlea lost.
statements.why: No hearing aid rebuilds the cochlea's level-dependent compression — which is why aggressive aid compression must be fitted carefully.

activities.anchor: Psychoacoustics measures the mapping between physical quantities and experiences
activities.caption: drag the divider — two tones, equal loudness
activities.name: hsLoudnessCompare

config.prompt: Equal loudness, unequal physics — drag between the two tones:

before.label: A 40 Hz tone
before.text: Needs far more pressure to sound equally loud — at low levels the ear is nearly deaf to deep bass.

after.label: A 2 kHz tone
after.text: Needs far less pressure for the same loudness — the canal's 2.7 kHz resonance lands right in this band.

config.why: Equal-loudness contours capture the ear's frequency-varying sensitivity — which is why equal-dB losses feel unequal across pitches, and why hearing aids are fitted per frequency band.

activities.caption: fit the aids — three programming philosophies
activities.name: hsAidBranch

config.root: A patient has a high-frequency slope on the audiogram. You are programming the hearing aids.

choices.label: Amplify everything uniformly
choices.feedback: Simple — and wrong for the frequency map.

choices.label: Amplify only where the loss lives, per frequency band
Skip the highs — vowels carry the energy anyway

uniform.text: Vowels (250–1,000 Hz) already arrive loudly; uniform gain overdrives healthy regions and distorts — the audiogram's slope is a per-band prescription.

perband.text: Amplifying only where the loss lives, leaving healthy regions alone: draw the patient's thresholds over the speech banana and the conversation becomes a picture of which sounds they are missing.

lows.text: Energy is not information: strip the consonants (4–8 kHz — the /s/ of 'six', the /f/ of 'five') and the vowel frames collapse together — clarity dies while loudness survives.

config.why: Speech does not spread its information evenly across the frequency axis — consonants are the information-bearing workhorses, and they live where the loss is.
